## 🎯 Objective · 🏁 Outcome {#objective}

::: {.bigline}
🎯 Create **reproducible content** you can **share with the world**, using Quarto.
:::

. . .

::: {.bigline}
🏁 Turn plain-text Markdown into **docx · pdf · pptx · xlsx · website · blog · dashboard**,
with the computations written by a coding assistant.
:::

::: {.notes}
Audience: people comfortable with files and a terminal, new to Quarto. Prerequisites:
Quarto, Python, Git, a GitHub account and one coding assistant installed (setup slide).
Completion: a published London dashboard URL and a published water-quality site.
The slides are the course resource: participants can follow them alone. Most steps
are done by prompting the coding assistant; the green boxes are the few things people
type themselves.
:::

# 🧭 What is Quarto? {#what-is-quarto}

[⏱️ 0:05]{.clock}

## Quarto = Markdown → anything {#quarto-hub}

![](assets/quarto-hub.svg){fig-alt="Two inputs, a .md Markdown file and a .qmd file with Python code, flow into Quarto (Pandoc plus Jupyter), which produces docx, pdf, pptx, an HTML website, a blog and a dashboard. A dashed arrow leads to xlsx." width="92%"}

[\* 📗 xlsx is not a Quarto format: a code cell writes it during the render
(e.g. pandas `to_excel`), and the page links to it.]{.source}

::: {.notes}
Pandoc converts the Markdown; Jupyter runs the Python cells and inserts their results.
Quarto's output formats include HTML, Word (docx), PowerPoint (pptx), PDF via Typst
or LaTeX, websites, blogs and dashboards: https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/all-formats.html
(checked 2026-10-30). Spreadsheets are not an output format, hence the dashed arrow.
:::

# 🛠️ Setup {#setup}

[⏱️ 0:10]{.clock}

## 🛠️ Setup check {#setup-check}

::: {.you}
```bash
quarto check
python --version
git --version
gh auth status
claude --version     # or: codex --version
git clone https://github.com/project-delphi/quarto-workshop.git
```
:::

📕 PDF: we use `format: typst`, which is bundled with Quarto (no LaTeX).
Prefer LaTeX? `quarto install tinytex`.

### Exercise · ⏱️ 5 min

::: {.done}
every check is green and `quarto-workshop/checkpoints/` exists.
:::

::: {.notes}
`quarto check` reports Pandoc, Typst and Jupyter. If Python has no Jupyter, ask the
coding assistant to set up a local environment and record the command; do not debug
kernels on stage. The cloned workshop repository supplies the checkpoints and the
water data. `gh auth status` must show a logged-in account before publishing.
Typst: https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html; TinyTeX:
https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/pdf-engine.html (checked 2026-10-30).
:::

Do this before the workshop. Sign in with an account that has access to the tool.
Claude Code installer: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup. Codex npm package:
https://github.com/openai/codex (README, checked 2026-10-30). Start the assistant
inside the exercise folder, and never run two assistants writing to one folder.
:::

## 🧰 Three boxes, three roles {#three-boxes}

::: {.prompt}
```text
Create london.md with a level-1 heading "Visit London" and one welcome paragraph.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
writes `london.md` · may run `quarto render london.md`
:::

::: {.you}
`quarto render london.md` → open `london.html`
:::

::: {.notes}
Violet: paste this prompt into your coding assistant (use the copy button).
Amber: what the assistant will probably run; you do not repeat it. Green: the few
things you type or click yourself, such as accounts, publishing and opening files.
The prompts are examples, not transcripts: assistants vary, so check the result.
:::

## 🗣️ How to prompt your coding assistant {#how-to-prompt}

::: {.cards}
::: {}
[🎯]{.big}

**Be specific**

file names, columns, chart types
:::
::: {}
[👣]{.big}

**One step at a time**

one task per prompt
:::
::: {}
[✅]{.big}

**Ask it to run & check**

"…render it and tell me about errors"
:::
::: {}
[👀]{.big}

**Read the diff**

you own the result
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
A good prompt names the file, the content, the output and a completion check.
Short follow-ups work once the conversation has context. Ask the assistant to show
what it changed; read the diff before moving on.
:::
